questions.q: What are the three most noticeable physical changes that occur during adolescence?
questions.a: The three changes are increase in height, increase in weight, and change in overall body shape. A wrong answer here suggests the student is confusing adolescence with general childhood growth or focusing on minor changes like hair or skin rather than structural body changes.

questions.q: Why does a teenager's weight typically increase during a growth spurt?
questions.a: Weight increases because of the development of larger bones and increased muscle mass. If a student says "only because of eating more food," they are missing the biological fact that the body's internal framework (bones and muscles) is actually getting heavier and denser.

questions.q: If a student grows 5 cm in two months, what is happening to their bones?
questions.a: The growth plates in the long bones of the arms and legs are responding to signals to add new bone tissue, causing the bones to physically lengthen. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks bones just "stretch" like rubber bands, rather than growing through the addition of new tissue.

questions.q: Why is the rapid change in height called a "growth spurt"?
questions.a: It is called a "spurt" because the lengthening happens very rapidly, often over just a few months, rather than at the slow, steady pace seen in childhood. An incorrect answer indicates the student does not understand that adolescence is a phase of accelerated, non-linear growth.

questions.q: Is it normal for body shape to change significantly during adolescence? Why?
questions.a: Yes, it is normal because the skeleton and muscles are reshaping to accommodate an adult-sized body. A student saying "no" or "only if you exercise" fails to realize that structural reshaping is a natural, biological process of maturation.

questions.q: Design a simple way to track your own physical changes over the next three months without using complex medical equipment.
questions.a: A good answer involves measuring height against a wall mark and recording weight on a scale at the same time each month. A poor answer would suggest tracking things that don't reflect structural growth, such as "counting how many hours I sleep" or "measuring the length of my hair."

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Physical changes in adolescence refer to the rapid, visible growth and ______ of the body's structure, including height, weight, and overall body shape, marking the transition from childhood to adulthood.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever looked at old photos of yourself from four ______ ago and realized your favorite shirt doesn't fit anymore?
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify the three primary physical changes (height, weight, body shape) and explain that these are outward signs of internal bodily growth.
